key_insight: This paper replaces the usual “generate-then-compress” 3D Gaussian Splatting pipeline with a feed-forward feature coding approach, making multi-view reconstruction and compression more efficient and learnable end-to-end. It aims to avoid separate, non-differentiable handling of geometry and appearance attributes.
problem_solved: Existing feed-forward 3DGS methods reconstruct a full Gaussian scene first and compress it afterward, which is cumbersome, non-differentiable in parts, and requires separate codecs for different attributes. The paper addresses the need for a simpler, more integrated way to encode 3D scenes from sparse views.
method: Uses a feed-forward multi-view feature coding pipeline to directly learn compact scene representations from sparse multi-view images.
Integrates geometry and appearance encoding more tightly, reducing reliance on separate attribute-specific compression stages.
Designed to better support differentiable learning and efficient reconstruction in a single forward pass.
impact: For practitioners, this could simplify 3D scene reconstruction pipelines while improving efficiency and deployability. It is especially relevant for applications where fast scene understanding and compact 3D representation matter, such as AR/VR, robotics, and view synthesis.

paper_title: Feed-Forward Multi-View Feature Coding for 3D Gaussian Splatting
